input.question: Does putting two engines on the same aircraft give it double the thrust?
input.ground_truth: Yes, thrust will double so long as the engines are far enough apart to avoid interacting with each other. Acceleration, top speed and other proformance indicators will not double and may even decreace due to the added weight and drag of a second engine however.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy car, and you put two motors on it. When you turn on one motor, the car goes zoom! If you turn on both motors at the same time, the car goes zoom-zoom even faster! But… it’s not exactly double the speed, because the car might get heavier and things like that can make it not go exactly twice as fast.

For airplanes, it’s a little like that. If you put two engines on the same plane, each engine can push the plane forward. So together, they can give the plane more push (that’s called thrust). But it’s not always *exactly* double the push, because the plane has to carry the weight of both engines, and sometimes the engines might not work perfectly together. But mostly, two engines can give the plane almost double the push to go faster or carry more stuff!
